classification.difficultyReason: Represent city selection before two responses, retain the same city's approval rate for both electors, combine weighted city-specific probabilities, and use the complement for at least one approval.

content.prompt: An interviewer conducts a poll in Sydney and Melbourne on the popularity of the prime minister. In Sydney, 52% of the population approve of the prime minister, and in Melbourne her approval rating is 60%. If one of the two capital cities is selected at random and two electors from that city are surveyed, find the probability that:

children.label: a
children.prompt: both electors approve of the prime minister,

answer.worked:
Assume the electors' responses are independent within each city.

The stages are city, first elector and second elector. Each city has probability 0.5; approval probabilities are 0.52 in Sydney and 0.60 in Melbourne.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{both approve})&=P(\text{Syd, Approve, Approve})+P(\text{Mel, Approve, Approve})\\P(\text{both approve})&=(0.5)(0.52)(0.52)+(0.5)(0.6)(0.6)\\P(\text{both approve})&=31.52\%\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: City, first elector and second elector, with every conditional branch labelled.
spec.mathematics: P(AA)=0.5(0.52)^2+0.5(0.60)^2=0.3152. Electors independent conditional on city.

children.label: b
children.prompt: at least one elector approves of the prime minister.

inlines.latex: \begin{aligned}P(\text{at least one approves})&=1-P(\text{both disapprove})\\P(\text{at least one approves})&=1-\bigl(P(\text{Syd, Disapprove, Disapprove})+P(\text{Mel, Disapprove, Disapprove})\bigr)\\P(\text{at least one approves})&=1-\bigl((0.5)(0.48)(0.48)+(0.5)(0.4)(0.4)\bigr)\\P(\text{at least one approves})&=80.48\%\end{aligned}
